survivingClaim: Given the recalled Gelfand-Tsetlin recipe for the double cover (n=2), at an unramified odd place with chi(-1)=+1: in unitary normalisation every pattern weight is a product of 1, 1-1/q, -1/q and T q^(-1/2). So the quadratic symbol T occurs only together with q^(-1/2) and every minus sign only together with q^(-1), in every rank (Lemma L; independently confirmed in rank 2 on new shapes and in rank 3). Row series in either twist direction satisfy the degree-3 recurrence with parameters (1, Yu^2, Xu^2 Yu^2) (confirmed for fixed label up to 4). For l1=0, l2 even the numerator equals the displayed product, and its only U-dependent term above order 1/q is -T Yu q^(-1/2) U. Epsilon factors of quadratic twists of any GL(n) form are a character times a periodic root of unity (no Jacobi-type value). No local term of the form (T-dependent sign) x (unit) occurs at order q^0. Not established: the numerator shape for other labels, any global Euler-product statement, the case chi(-1)=-1, the normalisation convention that turns Lemma 1 into an obstruction, and the global Whittaker constants of a genuine cusp form. No ledger entry with h>1. No statement about zeros.

lesson: The absorption criterion reduces to a weight table on the exponent group of the cover: Z/2 has no pair (a, b) with a, b, a+b all nonzero, so no double cover of any rank gives mu at shift 0 through local data. For twist families the cocycle is the n-th power of the GL(1) cocycle, so changing the automorphic form changes nothing.
